page_summary:
"The Empire Never Ended – But It Did Get a Makeover" is a presentation prepared by Don Dulchinos for the PKD Festival in Fort Morgan, Colorado, in Summer 2024. Subtitled "Gnostic impressions," the piece examines one of Dick's most famous recurring ideas: the concept that the Roman Empire never truly ended.

Dulchinos connects Dick's premise in VALIS and the Exegesis to Thomas Pynchon's similar exploration in Gravity's Rainbow (written ten years after The Man in the High Castle), where World War II is treated as an ongoing condition rather than a historical event with a definitive conclusion. The presentation explores how Dick's Gnostic vision of hidden imperial power structures persisting beneath the surface of apparent historical change has been updated and reinterpreted in contemporary contexts.

This document represents the intersection of Dick's philosophical ideas with contemporary political and cultural analysis, showing how his concept of concealed power structures continues to resonate with audiences decades after his death. The PKD Festival setting indicates an audience of engaged Dick scholars and enthusiasts.

## **THE EMPIRE NEVER ENDED – BUT IT DID GET A MAKEOVER Gnostic impressions prepared for PKD Festival, Fort Morgan, Colorado - Summer 2024 Don Dulchinos – dopod@indra.com** 

Just as _The Man in the High Castle_ is premised as if World War 2 never ended (as did Thomas Pynchon ten years later in Gravity’s Rainbow) Philip K. Dick wrote in _Valis_ and the _Exegesis_ that "the (Roman) empire never ended.”  A very viable take on the matter given the geopolitical state of the world today, some 40 years after PKD. The American Empire has not ended, rather is immanent. (USA-China-Saudi Arabia-Central Africa-Russia are all interpenetrated.) 

PKD’s quest, embodied in The Exegesis, took place with a foundation in his Berkeley/countercultural perception of the American Empire, but evolving and flowering in his perception of the present “laminated” onto the time of Christ. But his extraordinary efforts to arrive at some neo-Gnostic system took place, I believe, with the limitations of scholarship that was at the time of his studies about to be revolutionized by the full publication of the Nag Hammadi scrolls. I believe he anticipated the revision of understandings of Gnostic thought from God as Alien God, demiurge, etc., to a modern Gnostic take of “God as Man”. 

The PKD timeline vis-à-vis Gnosticism scholarship: 

- _The Gnostic Religion_ , Hans Jonas, 1958. 

- _The Nag Hammadi Library in English_ , James Robinson, 1977 

- _The Gnostic Gospels_ , Elaine Pagels, 1979 

- _Valis_ , Philip K. Dick, 1978 

“Gnosis consists of instructions that disinhibit the memory.” 

“The true living God is man himself.” 

This contribution will continue with a few quotes from the Gnostic Gospel of Thomas, the author’s 1983 table of correspondences between the three volumes of the _Valis_ trilogy, and close with some notes from the author’s book _Forbidden Sacraments_ , juxtaposing the historic shamanic uses of psychedelics (including their likely use by various Gnostic sects) with PKD’s Gnostic quest which was clearly informed by PKD’s usage of psychedelics, just as that usage first inspired or informed several of his more well-known novels. 

_**Note - This contribution forms the outline of what the author hopes will be a more fully elaborated submission to PKD Otaku in 2025.**_
